Title: Pure-tone sensitivity of human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones presented monaurally via earphone
Outcome: Infant pure-tone thresholds 10-30 dB higher than adults, greatest difference at 8000 Hz
Evidence_Quote: Pure-tone thresholds at frequencies ranging from 250 to 8000 Hz were estimated for 3-, 6-, and 12-month-old infants and for adults, using the Observer-based Psychoacoustic Procedure (OPP).

Title: Binaural unmasking in infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: broadband noise signal; broadband noise masker
Outcome: localization responses
Evidence_Quote: Localization responses to a broadband noise signal presented against a broadband noise masker were obtained from 12-month-old infants and adults.

Title: Suppression tuning curves for spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants (at 3 weeks, 2 months, and 3, 4, or 6 months of age)
Stimulus_Type: N/A
Outcome: suppression tuning curves; spontaneous otoacoustic emissions
Evidence_Quote: Suppression tuning curves (STCs) for spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) were longitudinally obtained in seven infants (at 3 weeks, 2 months, and 3, 4, or 6 months of age) and in five adults.

Title: Acoustic observations in young children's non-cry vocalizations.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: N/A
Outcome: harmonic doubling; fundamental frequency shift; biphonation
Evidence_Quote: A corpus of 1200 non-cry vocalization samples produced by 14 normal children between the ages of 11-25 months was examined retrospectively.

Title: Immunocytochemical and quantitative studies of Na+,K+-ATPase distribution in the developing chick cochlea.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: N/A
Outcome: Na+,K+-ATPase distribution
Evidence_Quote: Immunocytochemical methods were used to examine cryosections of the embryonic and neonatal chicken cochlea in order to study the histological distribution of the Na+,K+-ATPase molecule during maturation.

Title: The maturation of the central auditory conduction in preterm infants until three months post term. II. The auditory brainstem responses (ABRs).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 65 preterm infants (serial recordings up to three months post term)
Stimulus_Type: auditory brainstem response (ABR) test stimuli at 70 dB
Outcome: ABR component detectability at 70 dB reached 80-100% at about 32 weeks conceptional age; thresholds decreased with age
Evidence_Quote: The detectability of the different components in the ABR tests at 70 dB reached 80-100% at about 32 weeks CA.

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human adults and infants: wave V tuning curves.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: third-octave-filtered click probes with simultaneous tonal maskers (ABR wave V tuning curves)
Outcome: Infant and adult tuning curves similar for the 1.0-kHz probe; infant high-frequency tuning broader (smaller tip-to-tail difference, lower Q10)
Evidence_Quote: Probe stimuli were 1.0, 4.0, and 8.0-kHz third-octave-filtered clicks.

Title: Acoustic analyses of infant fricative and trill vocalizations.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: infant fricative and trill vocalizations (acoustic analysis; no presented stimulus)
Outcome: Infant fricative spectral components at and above 14 kHz; trill rate 16-180 Hz (mean about 100 Hz), about four times the adult rate
Evidence_Quote: Compared to similar fricative sounds in adult speech, the fricative sounds of the 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-month-old infants had primary spectral components at higher frequencies, i.e., to and above 14 kHz. Trill rate varied from 16-180 Hz with a mean of about 100, approximately four times the mean trill rate reported for adult talkers.

Title: The maturation of the central auditory conduction in preterm infants until three months post term. III. The middle latency auditory evoked response (MLR).
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: sound stimulation
Outcome: middle latency auditory evoked response
Evidence_Quote: Middle latency auditory evoked responses (MLRs) were recorded in 64 premature infants; serially in 54 of them.

Title: Infant speech-sound discrimination testing: effects of stimulus intensity and procedural model on measures of performance.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds /ba/ vs /da/ at three intensity levels
Outcome: Discrimination performance changed significantly with stimulus intensity
Evidence_Quote: Performance of infants in a speech-sound discrimination task (/ba/ vs /da/) was measured at three stimulus intensity levels (50, 60, and 70 dB SPL) using the operant head-turn procedure.

Title: Discrimination in neonates of very short CVs.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: shortened CV syllables
Outcome: discrimination of place of articulation; discrimination of vowel quality
Evidence_Quote: The experiment reported here explores the ability of 4- to 5-day-old neonates to discriminate consonantal place of articulation and vowel quality using shortened CV syllables

Title: Level and age effects in infant frequency discrimination.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones
Outcome: Infant FDLs worse than adults' and increased with frequency; FDLs increased at lower sensation level
Evidence_Quote: Frequency difference limens (FDLs) were estimated for 3-, 6-, and 12-month-old infants and for adults using pure tones at 500, 1000, and 4000 Hz. Each listener provided an FDL at 40 dB and at a higher (80 dB, in most cases) sensation level (SL).

Title: Infants' localization of sounds in the median sagittal plane: effects of signal frequency.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: bandpass noise bursts (low-pass less than 4 kHz, 4-8 kHz, 8-12 kHz)
Outcome: MAA decreased with age; best performance for the highest-frequency band (8-12 kHz); low-pass signal not reliably localized
Evidence_Quote: For each of three bandpass noise conditions (less than 4 kHz, 4-8 kHz, 8-12 kHz), minimum audible angle (MAA) for each listener, i.e., the smallest of the four angular shifts in vertical sound location that the listener could reliably detect, was estimated.

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human adults and infants: restriction of frequency contribution by notched-noise masking.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli with simultaneous notched-noise maskers (notch centers 1.0, 4.0, 8.0 kHz)
Outcome: Wave V latency/amplitude similar for adults and infants within the 1.0-kHz notch; group differences at higher notch frequencies
Evidence_Quote: Notch center frequencies were set at 1.0, 4.0, and 8.0 kHz. Responses were obtained at 20, 40, and 60 dBnHL during the simultaneous presentation of each notched-noise masker as well as in an unmasked condition.

Title: The blood flow velocity waveform in the fetal descending aorta; its relationship to behavioural states in the growth-retarded fetus at 37-38 weeks of gestation.
Journal: Early human development
Stimulus_Type: N/A
Outcome: blood flow velocity waveform; pulsatility index; fetal heart rate; behavioural states
Evidence_Quote: In 12 patients with intrauterine growth retardation (IUGR), the relationship between the blood flow velocity waveform at the lower thoracic level of the fetal descending aorta and fetal behavioural states at 37-38 wk of gestation was studied.

Title: Abnormal fetal behavioural state regulation in a case of high maternal alcohol intake during pregnancy.
Journal: Early human development
Stimulus_Type: N/A
Outcome: fetal behavioural state organization
Evidence_Quote: The present case report describes abnormal fetal behavioural state organization found in combination with maternal alcohol abuse during pregnancy.

Title: Masking effects on ABR waves I and V in infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 4-kHz tone pip with high-pass and low-pass maskers
Outcome: Masking patterns for ABR waves I and V differed between infants and adults, largest difference for wave I
Evidence_Quote: The signal was a 4-kHz tone pip presented at 86 dB peak equivalent sound-pressure level (p.e.SPL).

Title: Perception of syllable timing by prebabbling infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: alternating syllables; clicks
Outcome: time to habituate; sucking times
Evidence_Quote: In experiment 1, infants showed differences in time to habituate to sequences of alternating monosyllables, [bad] and [strad], having two different onset-onset times

Title: Infants' discrimination of final syllable fundamental frequency in multisyllabic stimuli.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: synthetic multisyllabic speech stimuli with final-syllable F0 increments relative to a 150-Hz standard
Outcome: Above-chance discrimination of F0 increments of 5-30 Hz relative to the 150-Hz standard
Evidence_Quote: Discrimination performance was above chance expectation for increments of 10, 20, and 30 Hz relative to a 150-Hz standard.

Title: Use of resonating cavity to measure body volume.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: N/A
Outcome: body volume
Evidence_Quote: A technique to estimate the body volume of newborns has been developed using the principle of the Helmholtz resonator.

Title: Infant pitch perception: evidence for responding to pitch categories and the missing fundamental.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic tonal complexes signaling two pitch categories (fundamentals 160 and 200 Hz)
Outcome: Infants categorized harmonic complexes by pitch, including complexes with the fundamental removed (missing fundamental)
Evidence_Quote: In the present study 7-8-month-old infants demonstrated the ability to discriminate harmonic complexes from two pitch categories that differed in pitch by approximately 20% (e.g., 160 vs 200 Hz).
